answer: A staking pool resists Sybils by requiring each new agent to lock a deposit that grows with every identity sharing the same funding source, like a lotus that opens only after its roots sink deep: one honest agent pays once and earns the bond back through verified work, while a faker must pay again for each clone. Misbehavior burns the bond and sends a ripple of distrust through the funding graph, and the forfeited stake is scattered like an ember that can never be rekindled into a fresh identity. Forging a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand rising deposits.
